messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Re: RApache getting stuck
parts:
Jeroen, I finally figured this out! Forget about editing apache2ctl
and forget about fiddling with ulimit.

To set per R session memory limits, use the function mem.limits()!
Here's an rapache handler which I used to test with:

handler <- function(){
setContentType('text/html')
# Only use 50Mb of memory
mem.limits(vsize=50*1024*1024)
cat("<h1>BigMem Test</h1>")
if (!is.null(GET$N)){
cat("<p>N=",GET$N,"</p>")
cat("<pre>")
x <- rnorm(as.integer(GET$N))
str(x)
cat("</pre>")
cat("object size says ",object.size(x)/1024/1024," Mb")
}
OK
}
and the apache2 config snippet:

<Location /R/bigmem>
SetHandler r-handler
RFileHandler /home/hornerj/bigmem.R::handler
</Location>


So when I surf to http://localhost/R/bigmem?N=6000000

I get

BigMem Test

N= 6000000

num [1:6000000] -1.33 1.216 -0.22 -0.236 0.631 ...

object size says 45.77639 Mb

But I'll get an Internal Server Error if N=7000000

Not an elegant way to fail, but at least using mem.limits() won't kill
your server.

Jeff

On Fri, Jan 22, 2010 at 4:58 PM, Jeroen Ooms <jeroe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Can I use this to impose time limits too, or would that mess up the
> recycling of the R sessions?

> On Fri, Jan 22, 2010 at 2:51 PM, Jeffrey Horner
> <jeffrey...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> Scope out the bash man page which has a section on using the function
>> ulimit. Then you'll want to edit your /usr/sbin/apache2ctl bash script
>> and add those commands. For instance the stock apache2ctl on my ubuntu
>> workstation has a configuration section that looks like this:
>>
>> # |||||||||||||||||||| START CONFIGURATION SECTION  ||||||||||||||||||||
>> # --------------------                              --------------------
>> #
>> # the path to the environment variable file
>> test -z "$APACHE_ENVVARS" && APACHE_ENVVARS='/etc/apache2/envvars'
>> # pick up any necessary environment variables
>> if test -f $APACHE_ENVVARS; then
>>  . $APACHE_ENVVARS
>> fi
>> # the following APACHE_* variables should be set in /etc/apache2/envvars
>> #
>> # the path to your httpd binary, including options if necessary
>> HTTPD=${APACHE_HTTPD:-/usr/sbin/apache2}
>> #
>> # a command that outputs a formatted text version of the HTML at the
>> # url given on the command line.  Designed for lynx, however other
>> # programs may work.
>> LYNX="${APACHE_LYNX:-www-browser -dump}"
>> #
>> # the URL to your server's mod_status status page.  If you do not
>> # have one, then status and fullstatus will not work.
>> STATUSURL="${APACHE_STATUSURL:-http://localhost:80/server-status}"
>> #
>> # Set this variable to a command that increases the maximum
>> # number of file descriptors allowed per child process. This is
>> # critical for configurations that use many file descriptors,
>> # such as mass vhosting, or a multithreaded server.
>> ULIMIT_MAX_FILES="${APACHE_ULIMIT_MAX_FILES:-ulimit -S -n `ulimit -H -n`}"
>> # --------------------                              --------------------
>> # ||||||||||||||||||||   END CONFIGURATION SECTION  ||||||||||||||||||||
>>
>> Add it just before that "END..." line".
>>
>> You would write:
>>
>> ulimit -d 100000
>>
>> which limits the data segment size to 100Mb
>>
>> Jeff
>>
>> On Fri, Jan 22, 2010 at 4:20 PM, Jeroen Ooms <jeroe...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>> http://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-patched/library/base/html/Memory-limits.html Is
>>> this something we could use instead? All my servers are 64bit.
>>>
>>> Unix
>>>
>>> The address-space limit is system-specific: 32-bit OSes imposes a limit of
>>> no more than 4Gb: it is often 3Gb or less. Running 32-bit executables on a
>>> 64-bit OS will have the similar limits: 64-bit executables will have an
>>> essentially infinite system-specific limit.
>>>
>>> See the OS/shell's help on commands such as limit or ulimit for how to
>>> impose limitations on the resources available to a single process. For
>>> example a bash user could use
>>>
>>> ulimit -t 600 -m 2000000
>>> whereas a csh user might use
>>> limit cputime 10m
>>> limit memoryuse 2048m
>>> to limit a process to 10 minutes of CPU time and (around) 2GB of memory.
>>>
>>>
>>>
>>>

>>>> Some minor insights about the RApache problem: I think the process
>>>> simply gets stuck when the machine runs out of memory.
>>>>
>>>> Yesterday someone visited my office and wanted me to try the ggplot2
>>>> webapp on his 1.000.000+ dataset. This is almost guaranteed to get
>>>> ggplot2 into problems. An empty plot would finish within the default
>>>> 40s time limit; a bin_2d would nicely give a timeout after 40seconds;
>>>> however, a density_2d would clog the machine almost instantly, because
>>>> of insufficient memory.
>>>>
>>>> Apparently, when the R process runs out of memory, it is not even
>>>> capable anymore of killing itself after the time limit has passed.
>>>> What would be needed is a way to limit the amount of memory per R
>>>> process, or set a timeout on the apache2 child process.
>>>>

parts:
On Tue, Jan 26, 2010 at 5:37 PM, Jeroen Ooms <jeroe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hey Jeff,
> thanks, this looks promising. Do I need to specify it in the form of a
> handler, or can I just prefix my existing Rscripts with a command
> like mem.limits(vsize=50*1024*1024), in the same way i set time limits?

A conservative strategy would be set mem.limits() using REvalOnStartup
. That way it gets set before any request is served. But you can call
that any time. Just remember that all handlers share the same R
interpreter in the same apache child process, so if you set
mem.limit() in one handler, like in my example, it will affect all
other handlers.

Jeff

> Jeroen
>
>
